cress can metabolize non-steroidal drugs and that the metabolites can be detected even at low drug levels in the water.

(i) the tested non-steroidal drugs are not toxic to the cress plant; (ii) the plant is able to metabolize the tested drugs, but only to a limited extent; and (iii) some of the formed metabolites are potentially harmful to human health.

the identification of metabolites formed from the four non-steroid anti-inflammatory drugs by cress and with the detection of the parent drugs as well as their metabolites at low concentrations in the plants grown in water containing the drugs.

the metabolism of non-steroidal drugs by plants and the potential of these plants to be used for the phytoremediation of reclaimed waters.

plants can metabolise non-steroidal drugs, but the extent of their metabolism depends on the type of the drug and its concentration.

the cress is able to metabolize all the tested drugs and that this process is not affected by the concentration of the drugs in the water, but the extent of the process is dependent on the chemical structure of the drug.

cress was able to metabolize all four non-steroid anti-inflammatory drugs, but at different rates and with different metabolic pathways.

cress is able to metabolize the tested drugs and that the plant extracts contain the parent drugs and metabolites in the same proportions as in the original solution.
cress can efficiently remove non-steroidal drugs from water and that this removal can be followed by the analysis of the parent components and metabolites.

cress grown hydroponically can be employed to remove non-steroidal drugs from water, as the plant efficiently metabolizes the parent drugs and the resulting products can be easily separated from the plant biomass.
